bullets.title: T: Solid 3Q Beat-and-Raise; Stock Down on SpaceX Wireless Threat
bullets.body: AT&T reported 3Q revenue of $32.30B (vs. $31.69B consensus), adj. EPS $0.65 (vs. $0.60 consensus), and EBITDA $12.51B (+5.4% y/y, beat). Wireless service revenue +5.0% y/y, fiber adds +442K total (beat), and FWA +327K; postpaid phone adds of 379K missed ~383-430K estimates. Management raised FY26 EPS guidance to ~$2.40 (from $2.25-$2.35), nudged EBITDA growth to upper portion of 3-4% range, and lowered 2027-28 capex to $22-23B from $23-24B. Stock initial -5-6% reaction attributed to SpaceX 2028 wireless entry commentary rather than fundamentals; Wolfe (Outperform, $29 PT), JPM (Overweight), UBS (Buy), and KeyBanc (Overweight, $36 PT) all maintain positive ratings.

bullets.title: NFLX: Q3 In-Line But Q4/Ad Guide Disappointment; Stock -6%; Mixed Analyst Reaction
bullets.body: Netflix Q3 revenue $12.87B in-line, EPS $0.87 beat ($0.82 consensus), operating margin 34.6% (+150bps beat), but Q4 revenue guided $13.44B (-0.6% vs. consensus) and EPS $0.67 (vs. $0.73 consensus) due to ~120bps headcount reduction impact. FY26 ad revenue guidance cut to $2.7B from $3.0B on slower ad product rollout and partner integration delays. Needham downgraded to Hold; Morgan Stanley keeps Overweight but cuts PT to $77 (from $80); Opco cuts PT to $80 (from $85); sell-side 65% buy avg PT ~$88. JPM flags NFLX as a popular short until Q4 earnings if 2027 revenue growth risks missing the '+10% Rubicon.'

bullets.title: SMCI: Massive Q1 Preannounce — Revenue $18.5-19.5B vs. $14.5-15.5B Guidance on AI Surge
bullets.body: Super Micro pre-announced FQ1 revenue of $18.5-19.5B vs. prior guidance of $14.5-15.5B and FactSet consensus of ~$14.9B, implying ~280% y/y growth; gross margins guided 12.0-12.5% vs. 10.4-10.8% prior guidance, with EPS tracking 60-70% above expectations. Upside attributed to strong AI platform demand and favorable customer/product mix; management reiterated $100B annualized revenue run-rate target by December. Stock up ~12-16% pre-market, lifting DELL (+6.8%), VRT (+6.5%), and broader AI infrastructure names.

bullets.title: NVDA: Massive Supply Chain Capacity Expansion Announced; Firmus Grid Investment Talks
bullets.body: NVIDIA announced multi-billion dollar capacity expansion agreements with Amkor, IBIDEN, KYEC, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, SPIL, and Unimicron — targeting substrate capacity +2.5x over three years, testing capacity doubling from 2026-2027, and SPIL optical engine capacity +15x by mid-2027 (doubling again by end-2028). NVIDIA also reportedly deployed $170B into neoclouds and is in talks to invest nine figures in Australia's Firmus Grid. Separately, Hedgeye removed its NVDA long citing Rubin mass production delay to Q2 2027 (vs. buyside expectation Q4 2026/Q1 2027) from four supply chain sources.

bullets.title: META: Earnings After Close Tonight; Buyside Bar High on 2027 Capex/Opex Guidance
bullets.body: META reports Q3 after close with stock up ~40% off lows on AI/Muse sentiment; JPM's buyside bar for 2027 opex is $210-225B (vs. Street ~$203B) and capex $225-250B (vs. Street ~$200B). Key debates: Muse engagement/retention metrics, personal agent competition, unit economics, and whether META may pursue an equity raise to fund accelerating AI capex. Mizuho sees near-term earnings compression from AI investment but maintains longer-term constructive view.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Earnings Pending; Cloud Upside Expected; OpenAI Models Now in Cloud Marketplace
bullets.body: GOOGL reports Q3 earnings (consensus EPS $3.03, revenue $127.92B) after close on Oct 28; Mizuho sees GOOGL positioned for near-term upside into results on positive cloud estimate revisions and cautious investor sentiment. Separately, Google announced OpenAI models (GPT-Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna) are now available in Google Cloud's model garden, allowing customers to draw down existing cloud commitments and swap models without vendor lock-in. Stock down ~1.1% pre-market on NFLX/T sympathy.

bullets.title: LITE: Jefferies Raises CY28 EPS to $44 (vs. Street $40.3) on GOOG OCS Demand
bullets.body: Jefferies is raising Lumentum CY28 EPS estimates to $44 vs. Street $40.3, driven by Google OCS demand and 1.6T exposure. Jefferies expects LITE to become GOOG's top OCS supplier in 2027, overtaking in-house production. JPM hosting post-earnings follow-up call with LITE management (CEO Michael Hurlston) on November 6.

bullets.title: GLW: JPM Previews 3Q Beat-and-Raise; PT Cut to $165 — Springboard Update Needed to Clear Buy-Side Bar
bullets.body: JPM expects Corning to beat 3Q26 estimates (revenue $5.04B vs. consensus $5.02B, EPS $0.90 vs. $0.88) driven by Optical-Enterprise momentum; 4Q26 also tracking ahead of consensus. However, JPM cut its PT to $165 (from $170) and maintains Neutral — meaningful upside requires a new 2028 Springboard target raise (mgmt targeting $30B, JPM models $27B) or DCI-2030 update. GLW reports Oct 27.

bullets.title: NET: Citi Reaffirms Buy, $400 PT; AI Agent Traffic +1700% YoY, Developer Base Accelerating
bullets.body: Citi reiterates Buy on Cloudflare with $400 PT, projecting 35%+ durable topline growth into/beyond CY27E vs. Street 28%. Developer base reached >10M in 3Q26 (vs. 7.4M in 2Q26), and AI agent traffic on NET's platform surged +1700% YoY. 78% of AI-native customers are gaining market share with rising multi-SKU uptake; Citi sees premium ~30x EV/S'27 valuation as justified given agentic AI positioning.

bullets.title: CRM: Acquires Braze at $47.50/sh ($5.7B); Strategically Sound but Organic Growth Questions Raised
bullets.body: Salesforce is acquiring Braze for $47.50 cash per share (~$5.7B EV, 5x CY27 revenues, 31x FCF) to strengthen its Marketing Cloud and AI capabilities (combining Braze mobile-first engagement with Data 360, Agentforce). UBS calls the deal strategically attractive but flags organic growth concerns; Braze downgraded to Neutral at UBS and D.A. Davidson post-announcement. Opco views positively for CRM's marketing franchise.

bullets.title: VRT: NVIDIA DSX Partnership Targets 30% More AI Token Output; Pre-Market Up ~6.5%
bullets.body: Vertiv introduced its AI factory approach combining NVIDIA DSX with pre-engineered reference architectures, targeting up to 30% more cumulative token output in the first 12 months with the same installed capacity. Polar Data Centers is applying the approach to a 41MW phase AI data center in Norway. VRT rallied ~6.5% pre-market in sympathy with SMCI's AI demand beat.

bullets.title: MU: Memory Stocks Down 42% from Peak; JPM Says Fundamentals Solid but 3Q Earnings Conviction Needed
bullets.body: Global memory shares (SEC/SKH/MU) have fallen ~42% from September 2026 peaks on AI capex funding concerns and neocloud CDS spread widening, with the market pricing in a potential down-cycle as early as 2027. JPM's bottom-up view is more constructive: spot prices trending upward, HBM ASP negotiation bias to the upside, and LTA order visibility extended. JPM says 3Q earnings results are the key catalyst needed to calm fears on AI capex sustainability.

bullets.title: SPOT: Earnings Due Oct 22; MS Upgrades to $640 PT; Buy Puts Flagged Pre-Print
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgraded Spotify to Overweight with a $640 PT, citing 15-20% streaming penetration runway and moderating opex growth from ~16% to ~8% in 2027. Separately, one desk flags buying SPOT puts ahead of 3Q print, expecting a miss on lower Premium ARPU, higher social charges, and 4Q gross margin pressure from audiobooks expansion. Consensus EPS €2.80, revenue €4.99B.

bullets.title: TSLA: SPCX Merger Special Committee Formed; Hedgeye Flips Bullish if Holds $375
bullets.body: Tesla and SpaceX boards formed special committees to explore a potential merger, with Elon Musk confirming interest on SPCX's earnings call. Hedgeye flipped TSLA trend from Bearish to Bullish, with trade level $370 and trend support $375; below that the $356 fractal is the break level. Historical context: TSLA crashed -33% in Q2-Q4 2026 and -74% in 2021-22 Q4 episodes. JPM raised SPCX PT to $500, adding TSLA as merger optionality narrative.

bullets.title: TXN: Reports Tonight; UBS Desk Expects High-End of Guide, Q4 Above Street
bullets.body: Texas Instruments reports tonight (consensus Q3 EPS $2.43, revenue $5.94B). UBS expects CQ3 revenue/EPS at the high end of guidance ($6.05B/$2.48) and CQ4 guidance of $5.8-5.9B above Street ~$5.7B, with data center growth tracking 73-75% y/y. TXN is positioned as an analog semi beneficiary of the broader rotation from crowded AI memory trades.

bullets.title: BKNG: EU DSA Investigation Opened on Fraud/Scam Mitigation Failures
bullets.body: The European Commission opened formal proceedings against Booking.com under the Digital Services Act, investigating whether the platform failed to adequately assess or mitigate risks from fraudulent listings and phishing scams. The Commission has authority to impose interim measures or non-compliance decisions. BKNG was flagged as under investigation in pre-market commentary.

bullets.title: ACN: Downgraded to Neutral at Baird; PT Raised to $252
bullets.body: Baird downgraded Accenture to Neutral from Outperform despite raising the PT to $252 from $245 (5% upside from $239). ACN was down ~1.1% pre-market in sympathy.

bullets.title: HPE: Partners with NVIDIA on Secure Agentic AI; Pre-Market Up ~6%
bullets.body: HPE announced new AI Factory with NVIDIA capabilities for secure autonomous AI deployment, including governed APIs, MCP services with versioning/audit trails, and enterprise-grade identity/governance with role-based access control. HPE is up ~6% pre-market in the SMCI/AI infrastructure sympathy rally.

bullets.title: NBIS: Launches Public Live Spot Pricing for GPU Compute
bullets.body: Nebius introduced public live spot pricing for GPU compute with multiple mechanisms: live preemptible spot pricing, reserve auctions for capacity blocks, and pay-as-you-go on-demand access. A capacity-rebate program allows customers to recover value by releasing idle GPUs back into the spot pool.

bullets.title: CRWV: Flagged as Top Short on Neocloud Financing Stress; Raised $34B at 15% Yield
bullets.body: CoreWeave raised $34B in equity and bonds at a 15% yield, raising counterparty exposure and neocloud leverage concerns. Hedgeye names CRWV as its #1 short on neocloud financing stress, and the desk flags potential uptick in GPU non-renewals/cancellations from neocloud operators. Separately, broader AI credit tail-risk protection costs are rising sharply, nearing equity put levels.
